editorialChecks.sourceScope: The article makes no changing product, price, regulatory, or platform claims, so no external source check applies. Loaded labor cost, overhead, and profit are explained as the reader's own bookkeeping inputs, not quoted figures.
editorialChecks.example: Fictional inputs: materials $300, waste 10%, crew hours 6, loaded cost $35 per hour, drive and setup 1 hour, overhead 15%, profit 20%. Expected display: quote $827, true cost $661, profit $165, gross margin 20.0%, effective rate $118.08 per hour, bars materials $330, labor $245, overhead $86, profit $165. Second case at 8% profit: quote $719 with the under-10-percent warning. Both labeled fictional; rounding to whole dollars explained.
editorialChecks.calculatorExampleCheck: Node imported the actual job-price-calculator tool from lib/tools and ran both input sets on 2026-09-16. Outputs matched the article text exactly: $827 / $661 / $165 / 20.0% / $118.08/hr and the 8% case at $719 with the verdict 'Under 10 percent profit, one bad day on this job wipes it out.'
editorialChecks.art: /og/tools/job-price-calculator.jpg inspected visually: 1200x630 navy card reading Job Price Calculator with the tagline Quote a job without guessing and a purple-topped notepad illustration. No event date or unrelated offer.
